title: EU egress matrix, policy precedence and emergency-deny workflow
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a precedence-driven egress policy matrix for EU-only routing and data-residency enforcement. Provide a clear emergency-deny path (customer/tenant-level denylist) and an allowlist capability for customers who require stricter routing. Tie policies into tier routing (hosted/dedicated/private) and fallback model variants so requests never leak out of permitted regions or tiers.
background: Multiple customers have asked for stronger guarantees that traffic and derived data never exit EU regions. Current geo-routing sends a preference but lacks a single source of truth for precedence between customer allow/deny lists, tier-based routing rules, and model-variant fallbacks. This gap risks non-compliant fallbacks during capacity pressure or runtime degradations.
goals: Define a deterministic precedence order for routing inputs (customer denylist > customer allowlist > contract-tier constraints > runtime fallbacks > global defaults)
Implement an egress policy decision module that returns a canonical route (region, tier, model-variant) and reason codes for observability
Expose admin controls for customers to manage allow/deny lists and view policy evaluation logs
Provide an emergency-deny workflow that can be triggered by infra or SRE to block cross-border routing during incidents
success_metrics: 0 policy violations in monthly compliance audits for customers with EU-only contracts
<1% fallback-induced egress to disallowed regions during peak load
Customer admin latency to update allow/deny takes <30s to become effective
Policy decision trace present for 100% of routed requests in observability pipeline
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine returns explicit reason_code and route tuple (region,tier,model_id) for every decision
Admin API for tenant allowlist/denylist: create/read/delete with audit log entries
Test harness simulating capacity pressure produces only allowed fallbacks per tenant policy
Emergency-deny toggle applied globally or per-tenant prevents any new routes to disallowed regions within 5s
End-to-end integration tests added to CI that validate full precedence matrix
technical_design: Introduce a lightweight Policy Decision Service (PDS) colocated with the routing gateway. PDS evaluates input keys in this order: tenant-denylist, tenant-allowlist, tenant-contract-tier, runtime-capacity-policies, model-compatibility-map, global-defaults. The output is a canonical Route object encoded as region:tier:model_id and a reason_code from a standardized enum. PDS will consult a cached store (strongly consistent for allow/deny entries) backed by CockroachDB + in-memory invalidation. Emergency-deny is implemented as a high-priority global flag in the cache with a CDC stream to all gateways. Gateways must reject decisions that contain region outside tenant's allowed set. We will add a compatibility mapping for model variants: when a preferred model is unavailable, PDS prefers same-region, same-tier quantized variant over cross-region fallbacks. If no compliant variant exists, PDS returns a BLOCKED decision and gateways surface HTTP 403 with a structured error. All policy evaluations emit traces and a compact policy_evaluation_id for later lookup.
implementation_tasks: Design policy precedence matrix and enumerate reason_code enum (doc: confluence/Geo/PDS-Precedence)
Schema: route tuple and policy_evaluation metadata; DB migrations for allow/deny tables
PDS service skeleton + REST gRPC API for evaluateRoute(tenant_id, requested_model, constraints)
Integrate PDS with gateway: sync protocol, caching TTLs, CDC for emergency flags
Admin UI+API for allow/deny management; RBAC hooks and audit entries
Model-variant compatibility engine: input model -> list of compatible variants (region/tier/quantization)
End-to-end tests: synthetic traffic harness with capacity stress to validate fallbacks
Observability: logs, traces, per-request policy_evaluation_id to console/trace UI
Fail-open/fail-closed policy for PDS outage (default: fail-closed for tenants with compliance flag, fail-open for non-compliant tenants with telemetry)
Emergency-deny orchestrator: admin endpoint + playbook for SRE + automated CDC propagation
rollout_steps: Canary PDS in eu-central region with 1% traffic using gateway routing override
Enable tenant allow/deny UI for internal compliance customers for manual testing
Gradually increase to 25% with automated smoke tests validating no disallowed egress
Open beta for customers that requested EU-only contracts; collect feedback
Flip default for new EU-only customers to enforced mode; monitor audits
Full rollout to all EU tenant traffic after 2 weeks stable with <0.1% policy errors
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: PDS outage might cause broad request failures. Mitigation: implement tiered fail strategy (fail-closed for EU-only tenants, fail-open with telemetry for others) and run chaos tests
Risk: Stale cache leading to policy gaps. Mitigation: CDC-driven invalidation, short TTL for allow/deny entries and strong consistency for write path
Risk: Complex precedence confusing customers. Mitigation: expose evaluation trace + human-readable explanation in admin UI and support playbook
Risk: Emergency-deny false positive. Mitigation: require two-person approval for tenant-level global emergency-deny and provide quick rollback steps
test_plan: Unit tests for PDS decision logic covering all precedence branches; integration tests with gateway and model-variant service; synthetic load tests that force fallbacks and verify no disallowed egress; chaos tests simulating PDS DB lag and verifying emergency-deny propagation. Add compliance smoke job that runs daily and asserts no cross-border routes for EU-only tenants.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Dashboards: policy_evaluation_rate, denied_by_emergency_deny, fallback_to_cross_region_percent, pds_error_rate. Alerts: pds_error_rate > 0.5% sustained -> page SRE; denied_by_emergency_deny spikes -> runbook execution. Add audit log retention 1 year for compliance tenants.
